findings.title: Reset code generated with non-cryptographic RNG
findings.description: random.randint() uses the Mersenne Twister PRNG, which is not cryptographically secure and can be predicted from other outputs. Password reset codes must be generated with a CSPRNG (e.g. secrets.randbelow) since predictability lets an attacker take over accounts.

findings.title: RESET_CODE_TTL_MINUTES is defined but never enforced
findings.description: The TTL constant is declared but reset_password() never checks how long ago the code was issued (the code/timestamp isn't even stored), so a leaked or guessed reset code remains valid indefinitely instead of expiring after 15 minutes.

findings.title: No rate limiting on reset code verification
findings.description: reset_password() allows unlimited attempts to guess the 6-digit code with no lockout/backoff, making brute-force of the ~1,000,000 possible codes feasible, especially combined with the missing expiry.

findings.title: Non-constant-time comparison of reset code
findings.description: `_reset_codes.get(username) != code` uses a standard string comparison instead of hmac.compare_digest, leaking timing information that could assist an attacker in a brute-force/timing attack against the code.

findings.title: Username enumeration via distinct error
findings.description: request_password_reset() raises AuthError('unknown user') when the username doesn't exist, letting an attacker enumerate valid usernames by observing the error response.

findings.title: In-memory reset code store is unsafe for production use
findings.description: _reset_codes is a plain module-level dict: it is lost on process restart, not shared across multiple worker processes (common in production deployments), not thread-safe, and grows unboundedly since entries for requested-but-never-completed resets are never removed or expired (memory leak / resource exhaustion).

findings.title: No tests added for password reset flow
findings.description: The PR adds two new public functions (request_password_reset, reset_password) with several edge cases (unknown user, wrong code, expired code, short password) but includes no accompanying tests to verify this security-sensitive behavior.
